description:
📕⚔️ Put a combat encounter into the BOOK for FUTURE games of this book (reuse). NOT a local edit of the current game's battle — this is the book's canon: the encounter will become available to the planner of any future playthrough. A repeat promote of the same textId OVERWRITES the book encounter (a deliberate decision).
        |When to call: you designed an encounter IN THIS turn (idea/tactical question/participants/terrain/stakes) with a reusable design — a battle worth pinning into the book. Promote IMMEDIATELY in the same turn you designed it: decisions do NOT make it into the book, the only channel into future games of this book is promote, a deferred promote = lost canon. You pass the whole object; the server checks its completeness (like the book pipeline's validator).
name: promoteToBookEncounter

encounter.description: Full encounter object (textId/name/description/idea/participants/tacticalQuestion/lossCondition/tactics/terrain/…). Passes the same completeness validation as the book generator.

name.description: Title (for analytics/UI): "Battle at the Crater's Edge", "Finale at the Anvil", "Ambush on the Way to the Island".

nodeTextId.description: textId of the node where it takes place. If null — the encounter is "floating", the planner can drop it in a suitable place.

description.description: Situation: who is here, what each side wants (a motive, not "they attack"), what will happen if the players do not intervene. 2-4 sentences.

idea.description: The battle's IDEA — the answer to "WHY does this battle exist at THIS point of the story": what is at stake, what the battle changes or reveals (the hero's arc, a twist, the price of a decision, the truth about the world). The setting, the enemy roster and spectacle are NOT the idea, they are decoration (`description` is about the SITUATION "who is here and what they want"; idea is about the MEANING of the battle in the plot). THE MAIN design field: the tactical question, the enemies' behavior and the stakes flow from the idea. An idea that is a scene description rather than a "why" → "a battle for the sake of a battle", a defect: perhaps the battle does not belong here.

participants.description: Encounter participants — enemies/neutral forces. At least 1.

profile.description: A profile WITHOUT NUMBERS: signature traits + relative danger in one or two phrases. "An elite shadow assassin — hits hard from stealth, fragile himself, relies on ambush". "A dim-witted brute — lots of health, slow, hits like a hammer". NO CR/HP/AC/damage — the turn master computes those to fit the party's strength.

scale.description: Relative scale of presence (NOT an absolute number): SOLO — a loner/boss; FEW — a small group; MANY — a noticeable crowd; SWARM — a swarm of minions. The exact number is chosen by the turn master to fit the player side's strength. Relative scale (no numbers): So=solo/boss; Fw=few/small group; Mn=many/crowd; Sw=swarm/swarm of minions.

role.description: Role in battle (exactly one word in Latin letters): "boss", "lieutenant", "minion", "support", "summon", "ally". This is the participant's canon, not an ornament: the turn master builds the enemy's role in battle from it, and "minion" is a minor role: a SWARM unit (one sheet represents a crowd) or a specific unit with its own role, not a clone extra. Set "minion" by its place in the battle, not as a filler by number.

motive.description: The participant's motive: what they want in this scene (besides "kill the heroes"). "Finish the ritual", "prevent escape", "hold out until help arrives", "protect the master". Makes behavior rounded, not just "attacks".

tacticalQuestion.description: **The main TACTICAL QUESTION** the battle puts to the player: "how to reach an enemy who is out of reach?", "how to protect an NPC while fighting?", "how to survive until reinforcements?". It is NOT the narrative reason for the battle ("bandits attacked") — it is the puzzle for the sake of which the battle exists. No tactical question → no battle is needed (reduce it to narrative/skip). Required (the validator rejects an empty one). See the "Battle construction" block.

primaryObjective.description: The party's main goal in the encounter beyond "kill everyone": disrupt a ritual, rescue captives, obtain an item, hold a position, win the crowd's favor. One sentence.

secondaryObjective.description: An additional optional objective (a tempting one): capture the lieutenant, obtain a document, keep an NPC from dying. Optional.

alternativeSolutions.description: At least 2 resolution paths besides combat: negotiation, deception, stealth, thwarting the plan, the environment, a bribe, a moral argument. Concrete, not "somehow get out of it".

terrain.description: Terrain with **four** traits: cover · movement obstacle · environmental hazard (hazards) · atmospheric detail. The best terrain contains all four.

tactics.description: **MUST BE FILLED IN** (null/blank is rejected by the validator). The opponents' tactics: how they fight, which combos they use, whom they attack first, at what HP they retreat/change behavior. 2-4 sentences, a description of behaviour, not a reactive strategy. Without tactics the encounter cannot be run by the turn master.

synergies.description: Explicit SYNERGIES between enemies "X reinforces Y" — where difficulty comes from (from the INTERACTION of roles, not from the sum of stat blocks): "the Controller roots the PC → the Artillery focuses them", "the Support enrages the Brute → an extra attack", "A places hazard terrain → B pushes into it with forced movement". Reference real participants by name/role. Two identical units are differentiated not by stats but by role (one holds the flank, the other pushes). NOT mechanically gated (a SOLO boss legitimately has no links) — checked by self-review. An empty list — only for solo bosses.

twist.description: Twist draft: reinforcements / a new danger / an unexpected reveal + a trigger condition. The generator writes a DRAFT — the decision to introduce it is made by the turn planner in real time. Optional.

event.description: What happens: enemy reinforcements, a roof collapse, a third party appearing, an ally's mask being revealed. 1-2 sentences.

trigger.description: Trigger condition: "the alarm is raised", "the battle lasts >5 rounds", "an NPC drops below 50% HP", "a rune is activated", "the party is close to victory". Precise at the end, so the planner understands when to introduce it.

stakes.description: Plot consequences of failure OUTSIDE the scene (not just a "rollback"): "the order's reputation falls", "the protagonist gets an artifact", "the village is left without protection", the BB speeds up the timeline. One concrete sentence. Differs from `lossCondition` (an observable trigger INSIDE the scene) — this is what will echo AFTER the battle.

lossCondition.description: The observable LOSS TRIGGER INSIDE the scene — a mechanical condition, and NOT necessarily a TPK: "the prisoner was carried out through the north exit", "the alarm is raised — reinforcements in 2 rounds", "the NPC ally was led away", "the party was bound and captured". Without a loss-condition the stakes are not real (the battle = an HP race to zero). Differs from `stakes` (consequences OUTSIDE the scene) — this is what fires RIGHT IN THE BATTLE. Required (the validator rejects an empty one).

arenaSupport.description: How the arena **physically supports** the primaryObjective. "An altar in the center with an approach from the right — for 'disrupt the ritual'", "4 doors on the perimeter — for 'hold the position'", "a staircase to the balcony for a stealthy flank". Optional (recommended for boss fights and important encounters). Linked via `nodeTextId → locationTextId`.

phases.description: Phases of a multi-phase battle (1c §3): "phase 1 — disable the shield, phase 2 — finish the boss", "ground → when the dragon is wounded, it flies off to a cliff, an aerial battle begins". Each phase has its own condition (when to switch) and effect (what changes). An empty list — a one-shot battle. Usually for boss fights and the climax.

name.description: Title: "Phase 1: disable the shield", "Phase 2: finish the boss", "Phase air: the dragon in the air", "Finale: forge collapse".

description.description: Phase description: what happens, what the task is, what the choices are. 1-3 sentences.

condition.description: Condition for transitioning into this phase. For the first — null/"battle start"; for subsequent ones — a concrete trigger: "when the boss's HP <50%", "when the shield crystal is destroyed", "after round 5", "when one of the minions ran off for reinforcements".

effect.description: What changes in the arena/encounter on switching: new opponents appear, hazards activate, access to a POI opens, terrain changes (the bridge collapsed). Concretely — what the planner must change in the scene.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description:
⚔️📝 RECORD THE BATTLE'S DESIGN — the first thing you do, and the frame for everything else.
        |The IDEA — the answer to "WHY this battle in the story": what is at stake, what the battle changes or reveals (in the plot, in the characters, in understanding the world). The setting, the enemy roster and spectacle are NOT the idea, they are decoration. No idea or no tactical question — no battle (the norm and what to do next are in the stage instruction).
        |The TACTICAL QUESTION — "how this battle plays": a puzzle for the player ("how to reach an enemy who is out of reach", "how to survive until reinforcements"). It is subordinate to the idea and reveals it through mechanics; the roster and synergies are assembled FOR IT, not the other way round.
        |A repeat call REWRITES the plan entirely (editing a live battle is not your tool: in an ongoing battle the plan is edited by the battle master).
        |The plan is persisted together with the battle: ALL its rounds will follow it, and it will be read by the battle master, who is absent from this pass.
name: setEncounterPlan

textId.description: Battle slug `[a-z0-9-]+`: a book encounter — under its textId (then future turns recognize the battle), your own battle — a new meaningful slug.

idea.description: The battle's IDEA — "why it is in the story": what is at stake, what it changes or reveals. Not decoration, not a retelling of the setting.

tacticalQuestion.description: Tactical question — "how it plays": a puzzle for the player stemming from the idea.

sideStrength.description: The player side's strength (S) in one phrase — the baseline against which the round volley's lethality is computed: "solo PC L4, no allies".

synergies.description: Enemy synergies "X reinforces Y" — the links from which difficulty is born ("the controller roots the target → the shooter focuses it"). Each must be expressed through the fighters' concrete abilities, otherwise it is decoration. Empty — only for a solo threat.

worldEventSeeds.description: 1-3 world-event drafts — the IDEA of an event, not "what will fall": what it will open, change or offer in the course of the battle. The battle master is free to adapt them to the table's realities.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description:
⚔️ DECLARE THE BATTLE ROSTER — the battle begins with this call and only it. List ALL its participants in ONE call: player characters, enemies, NPC allies.
        |🎲 THE INITIATIVE IS ROLLED BY THE SERVER, once per battle: from you — only the terms (Dexterity and sheet bonuses of each), the die and the queue order are computed by it. You will not see the roll numbers in this pass and must not write them — this is not a delay of the response but a division of labor: you know the rules, the server rolls the die.
        |The PLACE of each — on the grid of the current map: for one who already stands in the scene, do not name a cell (they stay where they stood), for one who comes into the battle — name it. You do not change the map: the battle goes where the scene already stands.
        |A repeat call REPLACES the previous roster ENTIRELY (this is a re-declaration, not an addition) — list everyone anew.
        |⛔ The battle is born at the END of the pass, together with the rest of your work: entering the battle as a single record yields the roster and the initiative order, the first turn is handed to a fighter by you. Therefore the call does not "launch" anything immediately and there is nothing to roll it back with except a new declaration.
        |Not calling at all is a LEGITIMATE outcome: you decided there is no battle (the "when there is no battle" norm is in the stage instruction) — finish without it, and the scene continues peacefully.
name: startBattle

combatants.description: The WHOLE battle roster: everyone who will enter the battle roster. A fighter omitted here does not take part in the battle, even if standing nearby on the map.

textId.description: textId of the fighter — a character of this game (ordered by you in this pass or already standing in the scene).

initiativeModifiers.description: The INITIATIVE terms of this fighter with labels (Dexterity and other bonuses from its sheet) — YOU compute them, the server rolls the d20. Do not write roll numbers here: you do not have them and will not have them in this pass.

description.description: Description of the modifier / bonus component (for example 'Prof', 'Strength', 'Guidance', 'Sneak Attack')

value.description: Value of a STATIC modifier (a flat bonus: +3 proficiency, +2 Strength). For a DICE component (diceType is set) do NOT fill in — the server will roll the die and write the rolled sum here (as a tool this is a server field: do not repeat it for a pinned slot).

diceType.description: Type of the bonus DIE, if this component is a die roll INSIDE a check/attack/damage (Guidance/Bless d4, Bardic Inspiration, sneak damage 2d6): D4/D6/D8/D10/D12/D20/D100. Set ONLY when the bonus is random. null — an ordinary static modifier (a flat number in value).

count.description: Number of bonus dice (2d6 sneak → diceType=D6, count=2). 1 by default. Meaningful only together with diceType.

position.description: The cell from which the fighter enters the battle. Leave empty for one who ALREADY stands on the grid (a player's character, a scene NPC) — they stay where they are; name it for one who comes into the battle (an ordered fighter, reinforcements), or when you move a fighter into the battle formation.

description: ORDER FIGHTERS from the character specialist — in ONE call for the whole roster the game lacks. You say WHO the battle needs and WHY (role in battle, tactical function, what makes them dangerous, how many); the sheet, stats, attacks, resources and look are assembled by the specialist — you do not create characters yourself and do not dictate mechanics. TWO LISTS: `newcomers` — those not yet in the game; `reinforcements` — already existing faces whose sheet needs BRINGING to battle standard (armor, a combat ability, a state on entry). Both go as ONE batch to one executor: in total no more than 6 positions per call, more is a SECOND batch. ⏳ There will be NO result in THIS response: the order is executed at the end of the response, the finished fighters will appear in the snapshot (the "📦 CHARACTER ORDERS" block) in the NEXT response — and then declare the battle roster (`startBattle`). Do not go into review in the same response: the transition will be rejected until the order has returned. A repeat call — a SECOND batch of fighters, not a reminder of the first. The specialist is entitled to DECLINE an individual order (the reason will come in the same snapshot) — then you decide: stage the battle without this fighter or do not stage the battle at all.
name: orderCombatants

newcomers.description: NEW fighters — one element per ROLE. Do not multiply elements for a same-type crowd: that is ONE element — either `scale=SWARM` (a crowd as ONE sheet: an HP pool, the "Swarm" trait, crowd damage), or `count` separate fighters whom the specialist will differentiate with distinctions (the series cap is 8).

role.description: Who this is to the scene — role/function in words: "innkeeper", "guard sergeant", "syndicate liaison".

request.description: The order in words: why the scene needs the face, what it is busy with, what stands out, what is known about it from the book and the master's decisions. Self-sufficient — your scene's specialist does not see it.

significance.description: SIGNIFICANCE — your decision, not the specialist's (the scale is in the "🎯 SIGNIFICANCE" block of your instruction): BACKGROUND — a nameless extra; MINOR — a passing face of this scene; MAJOR — a figure the story will return to; LEAD — a key face of the campaign. Be STINGY: both the depth of the sheet and the level of the portrayal depend on it.

presence.description: Whether the face is OFF-FRAME: OFFSTAGE — it is NOT in the scene, it keeps driving events from off-frame (the second entry of the materialization criterion) — the server will set standby status, no token is needed; ONSTAGE — stands in the scene, needs a token on the grid.

anyOf.description: Non-empty list of canonical observer UUIDs.

name.description: Name, if it ALREADY exists in the book or was heard in the game. null — the specialist will invent a name.

textIdHint.description: The BASE OF THE ADDRESS in Latin letters — a short role slug (`dock-foreman`, `tavern-keeper`). The server will pick a free address and return the actual one; Cyrillic cannot become an address, so without a hint the face gets a faceless `npc-2`.

count.description: How many IDENTICAL (by scale [scale]) units are needed. 1 — one unit; the series cap is 8, more is several orders for different roles.

scale.description: WHAT ONE unit of `count` represents: INDIVIDUAL — a separate creature with its own sheet (with count>1 the specialist will make series clones and differentiate them with distinctions — it does not stamp identical ones); SWARM — ONE sheet represents the WHOLE CROWD (an HP pool, the "Swarm" trait, crowd damage) — this is not a number but a stat block FORM: SWARM with count=2 means TWO crowds (for example, goblin squads from different flanks).

props.description: CANONICAL PROPS AS A LIST — items that must end up in their inventory ("a tube with papers", "a warehouse key", "a guild seal"): what is not in the sheet cannot be handed over, taken away or searched. Prose in the order text does not count — list them.

guidance.description: Recommendations: tone, origin, manner, place in the scene. Do not dictate mechanics (stats, hp, attacks) — that is the specialist's.

bookNpcTextId.description: Book CANON key: the textId of a figure from the adventure structure (`antagonist`/`keyNpcs`) OR a key from the "📕 CANONICAL BOOK NPC PROTOTYPES" block (the registry pinned by past games — it also has faces outside the structure), if you are ordering precisely that figure: the specialist will take the ready canonical prototype instead of molding anew. A face outside the book's canon — null.

reinforcements.description: ALREADY EXISTING fighters whose sheet needs bringing up to battle standard: textId and what exactly to fix. The sheet is not rebuilt — what is missing for the role in this battle is added.

textId.description: textId of an already existing character whose sheet needs adjusting for the battle (known to the game — including those not currently in frame).

request.description: The order in words: WHAT to fix in the sheet and WHY (armor before battle, tactical position, state at battle entry). Self-sufficient — the specialist does not see the request or the turn.

description: Record a new task for yourself as a result of self-review. Available ONLY in the SELF_REVIEW phase. After adding all tasks call transitionTo into the working phase — the frame will execute them there.
name: addTask

description.description: What exactly needs to be done

description: Mark the task as done. A REVIEW item (rev-*) is closed ONLY this way — one at a time, with a VERDICT in reason.
name: completeTask

reason.description: Verdict/reason for closing. REQUIRED for REVIEW items (rev-*): the specifics (textId/role/numbers/coordinates) on which the item settled, or a violation + the id of the fix task for it.

description: Mark several tasks as done in one call. Use for going through the working phase's checklist in a row (for example, closing several 'chk-*' items) when there are no intermediate decisions between them. If an idea appears along the way — close them one by one via completeTask. REVIEW items ('rev-*', the self-check phase) are NOT closed by this tool: each requires a separate completeTask with a verdict-specific in reason, batch closing is rejected.
name: completeTasks

ids.description: List of task IDs to close

description: Transition to another state (phase) of work. Call it once the current phase's work is complete — as the LAST call of the SAME response that finishes that work (when the phase rules allow the transition). The switch is applied at the END of this response: every other call in the same response still runs in the CURRENT phase, so it is safe to finish the phase's work and request the transition together. Do not spend a separate response on a lone transition call, and do not place new work AFTER the transition expecting the new phase.
name: transitionTo
